Long-necked tortoise.t: Wanjel: Long-necked tortoise. In the sky: Pollux.

Fan-tailed cockatoo.t: Yurree: Fan-tailed cockatoo. In the sky: Castor.

Two teenage boys.t: Kulkanbulla: Two teenage boys. In the sky: Belt and Scabbard of Orion.

Girls.t: Lamankurrk: Girls, young women. In the sky: Pleiades.

Red kangaroo.t: Purra: Red kangaroo. In the sky: Capella.

Ring-tail possum.t: Bunya: Ring-tail possum. In the sky: Top star in Southern Cross.
Ring-tail possum.o: The Boorong see in the Southern Cross a possum in a tree; Bunya is its top star.
Ring-tail possum.c: Wikipedia, “Australian Aboriginal astronomy”; Stellarium's Boorong sky culture

Red-rumped parrot.t: Djuit: Red-rumped parrot. In the sky: Antares.

Crow.t: War: Crow. In the sky: Canopus.
Crow.o: War the crow is Canopus. His wife, Collowgulloric War, is the star beside him now known as Eta Carinae.
Crow.c: D. W. Hamacher and D. J. Frew, An Aboriginal Australian record of the Great Eruption of Eta Carinae, Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage 13, 220 (2010)

Female crow, wife of War.t: Collowgulloric War: Female crow, wife of War. In the sky: Eta Carinae.
Female crow, wife of War.o: Hamacher and Frew argued in 2010 that this is Eta Carinae, and that the Boorong saw its great outburst of the 1840s, when it was for a while one of the brightest stars in the sky, and made it part of their tradition.
Female crow, wife of War.c: D. W. Hamacher and D. J. Frew, Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage 13, 220 (2010)

Owlet nightjar.t: Yerredetkurrk: Owlet nightjar. In the sky: Achernar.

Needlewood hakea and willie wagtails.t: Tourchingboiongerra: Needlewood hakea and willie wagtails. In the sky: Coma Berenices.

Red-kneed dotterel.t: Berm-berm-gle: Red-kneed dotterel. In the sky: Alpha and Beta Centauri.

Australian kestrel.t: Karik Karik: Spear thrower; Australian Kestrel. In the sky: Two stars at end of Scorpius.

Mallee fowl.t: Neilloan: Mallee fowl. In the sky: Lyra.
Mallee fowl.o: When Neilloan, the mallee fowl in Lyra, set just after dusk in October, the mallee fowl's eggs were ready to be gathered on Earth.
Mallee fowl.c: W. E. Stanbridge (1857), as summarised in Wikipedia, “Wergaia” and “Australian Aboriginal astronomy”

Jacky lizard.t: Unurgunite: Jacky lizard. In the sky: Sigma Canis Majoris.

Male and female brolga.t: Kourt-chin: Male and female brolga. In the sky: Clouds of Magellan.

Great fish.t: Otchocut: Great fish. In the sky: Delphinus.

Wedge tailed eagle.t: Warepil: Wedge tailed eagle. In the sky: Sirius.

Female eagle, wife of Warepil.t: Colowgulloric Warepil: Female eagle, wife of Warepil. In the sky: Rigel In Orion.

Purple crowned lorikeet.t: Totyarguil: Purple crowned lorikeet. In the sky: Altair.

Meat ant.t: Marpeankurrk: Meat ant; treecreeper. In the sky: Arcturus.
Meat ant.o: When Marpeankurrk, Arcturus, rose in the north at dusk, it was time to gather the larvae of the wood ant.
Meat ant.c: W. E. Stanbridge, On the astronomy and mythology of the Aborigines of Victoria, Transactions of the Philosophical Institute of Victoria 2, 137 (1857), as summarised in Wikipedia, “Wergaia”

Milky Way.t: Warring: Galaxy. In the sky: Milky Way.

Singing bushlark.t: Weetkurrk: Singing bushlark. In the sky: Star in Bootes west of Arcturus.

Pink cockatoo.t: Gellarlec: Pink cockatoo. In the sky: Aldebaran.

Species of ant.t: Collenbitchick: Species of ant. In the sky: Double star in head of Capricornus.

Boomerang.t: Won: Boomerang. In the sky: Corona Australis.

The maned snake.t: Mindi: The maned snake. In the sky: Part of the Milky Way.
